command:
set +e
set -uo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp MPLCONFIGDIR=/tmp/mpl
cd /tmp

# spawn runs task commands under bash -e and `set -uo pipefail` does not clear it
# (spawn#707), so errexit is cleared above and every status is checked by hand.

echo "== the bytes must match ENCODE's own published md5 before any compute =="
md5sum -c encode.md5 || { echo "FAIL: a BAM does not match ENCODE's published md5"; exit 1; }
echo "pin	both BAMs match ENCODE's published md5"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- inline instrument
# 1 Hz sampler of cgroup v2 + tmpfs, inline per measurements/sizing-ratio (no shared
# engine). Fail-soft: if cgroup is unreadable the fields read 0 and the wall clock and
# the science are still valid.
CG=/sys/fs/cgroup
echo "cgroup_v2_readable	$([ -r $CG/memory.current ] && echo yes || echo no)"
sampler() {
  : > /tmp/samples.tsv
  while : ; do
    mc=$(cat $CG/memory.current 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    an=$(awk '/^anon /{print $2; exit}' $CG/memory.stat 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    cu=$(awk '/^usage_usec/{print $2; exit}' $CG/cpu.stat 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    tk=$(df -k /tmp 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR==2{print $3}')
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$(date +%s)" "${mc:-0}" "${an:-0}" "${cu:-0}" "${tk:-0}" >> /tmp/samples.tsv
    sleep 1
  done
}
sampler & SPID=$!

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the real workload
# Whole genome, not chr20. Same two ENCODE files the shipped recipe subsets, same -f BAM
# and -g hs so the only thing that changed is the amount of data.
echo "== macs2 callpeak, whole genome =="
T0=$(date +%s)
macs2 callpeak -t ENCFF933NSJ.bam -c ENCFF768XTH.bam -f BAM -g hs -q 0.05 \
  -n real --outdir /tmp > /tmp/macs2.log 2>&1
RC=$?
T1=$(date +%s)
kill $SPID 2>/dev/null; wait $SPID 2>/dev/null
WALL=$((T1-T0))
echo "macs2_rc	$RC"
echo "macs2_wall_s	$WALL"
tail -5 /tmp/macs2.log
test "$RC" = "0" || { echo "FAIL: macs2 exited $RC"; exit 1; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the instrument's answer
awk -F'\t' -v wall="$WALL" '
  NR==1{cu0=$4}
  {if($2>mc)mc=$2; if($3>an)an=$3; if($5>tk)tk=$5; cu=$4; n++}
  END{
    printf "peak_rss_mib\t%.0f\n", mc/1048576;
    printf "anon_max_mib\t%.0f\n", an/1048576;
    printf "tmpfs_peak_mib\t%.0f\n", tk/1024;
    if(wall>0) printf "avg_cores\t%.2f\n", (cu-cu0)/(wall*1000000);
    printf "samples\t%d\n", n;
  }' /tmp/samples.tsv
cat $CG/memory.peak 2>/dev/null | awk '{printf "memory_peak_mib\t%.0f\n", $1/1048576}'

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- checks on the result
# An identity, not a band: macs2 was asked for q <= 0.05, so every row it reports must
# satisfy that. narrowPeak column 9 is -log10(q), so the floor is 1.30103. A truncated or
# mis-thresholded run fails this; a band on the peak count would not.
PEAKS=$(grep -vc '^#' /tmp/real_peaks.narrowPeak 2>/dev/null)
echo "peaks	${PEAKS:-0}"
test "${PEAKS:-0}" -gt 1000 || { echo "FAIL: only ${PEAKS:-0} peaks genome-wide"; exit 1; }

BADQ=$(awk -F'\t' '$0!~/^#/ && NF>=9 && $9 < 1.30103 {n++} END{print n+0}' /tmp/real_peaks.narrowPeak)
echo "peaks_below_q_cutoff	$BADQ"
test "$BADQ" = "0" || { echo "FAIL: $BADQ peaks are below the -q 0.05 cutoff macs2 was given"; exit 1; }

BADF=$(awk -F'\t' '$0!~/^#/ && NF!=10 {n++} END{print n+0}' /tmp/real_peaks.narrowPeak)
echo "rows_not_10_fields	$BADF"
test "$BADF" = "0" || { echo "FAIL: $BADF narrowPeak rows are malformed"; exit 1; }

# One summit per peak is a structural property of macs2's own output pair.
SUM=$(grep -vc '^#' /tmp/real_summits.bed 2>/dev/null)
echo "summits	${SUM:-0}"
test "${SUM:-0}" = "${PEAKS:-0}" || { echo "FAIL: $SUM summits for $PEAKS peaks"; exit 1; }

# Observation, deliberately NOT an assertion: the shipped chr20-only recipe reports 1390
# peaks. Restricting THIS run to chr20 cannot be expected to reproduce that, because the
# background lambda and the effective genome size both differ when the whole genome is in
# the model. Recorded so the difference is visible rather than surprising.
CHR20=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="chr20"' /tmp/real_peaks.narrowPeak | wc -l)
echo "chr20_peaks_in_wholegenome_run	$CHR20"
echo "chr20_peaks_in_shipped_chr20_recipe	1390"

{ echo -e "observable\tvalue"
  echo -e "macs2_wall_s\t$WALL"
  echo -e "peaks\t$PEAKS"
  echo -e "summits\t$SUM"
  echo -e "peaks_below_q_cutoff\t$BADQ"
  echo -e "chr20_peaks_wholegenome\t$CHR20"
} > /tmp/clock.tsv

nproc | awk '{print "nproc\t"$1}'
uname -m | awk '{print "arch\t"$1}'
echo "MACS2 REAL OK"
